comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
RCA update (2026-09-06 local macOS host; investigation only, no code changes):

Phase 1 — observed failure facts
- Current post-reboot high-RSS uv-cache Python processes are Serena MCP servers, not rebar-mcp and not rebar async gate daemons:
  - pid 7641, ppid 7628, rss ~1.34GB: `/Users/joeoakhart/.cache/uv/archive-v0/9qJ1RQgFru1NlHM-/bin/python /Users/joeoakhart/.cache/uv/archive-v0/9qJ1RQgFru1NlHM-/bin/serena start-mcp-server --context ide-assistant --project /Users/joeoakhart/rebar`
    - parent uv pid 7628: `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv tool uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena serena start-mcp-server --context ide-assistant --project /Users/joeoakhart/rebar`
    - owning harness chain is live Copilot CLI: `copilot --allow-all` pid 6590 -> uv 7628 -> Serena 7641.
  - pid 11266, ppid 11205, rss ~1.34GB: `/Users/joeoakhart/.cache/uv/archive-v0/0fc0W5v5AHQWhhQv/bin/python /Users/joeoakhart/.cache/uv/archive-v0/0fc0W5v5AHQWhhQv/bin/serena start-mcp-server --context codex --project-from-cwd`
    - parent uv pid 11205: `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/uv tool uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@c7dbe3bd1198cf451bf7aa8fdeeab88571fa3a6e serena start-mcp-server --context codex --project-from-cwd`
    - owning harness chain is live Codex under ChatGPT: `.../headroom wrap codex` -> `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/.../codex` -> uv 11205 -> Serena 11266.
- These Serena servers each spawn pyright through another uvx wrapper. Example pid 7641 children: uv 7650 `uv tool uvx -p 3.13 --from pyright==1.1.403 pyright-langserver --stdio`, Python shim 7651, node pyright 7655.
- lsof shows the MCP stdio pipes are still open at both ends while the harness lives. Example for Copilot: Serena 7641 fd0/1/2 are PIPEs; uv 7628 has the same fd0/1/2; Copilot pid 6590 holds peer pipe fds 41/57/59. Therefore no EOF can be delivered while Copilot retains those fds.
- sample(1) of high-RSS Serena pid 7641: physical footprint 1.3G. Main thread is parked in Python selector `kevent`; three worker/reader threads are blocked in `_buffered_readline`/`_io_FileIO_readinto`/`read`; other threads are sleeping or waiting on locks. This is an idle stdio MCP server waiting for input, not a CPU spin.
- Converted shutdown-stall spindump corroborates the same shape before reboot: large `python3.13` processes under `/Users/joeoakhart/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.13.5.../bin/python3.13`, parented by uv. The large ones were ~1100-1168MB. Crucially, many root uv parents were parented by an orphaned Copilot process, not by a live terminal: `Process: copilot [38798]`, parent `launchd [1]`, footprint 9412.51MB, age 455249s. Representative uv parents: 38999/42587/42630/72616/17326/5909/79810/76220/7243 all parented by copilot 38798; each had a large Python child. A smaller Claude-owned case also existed near shutdown (`2.1.261` -> uv 87245 -> python 87538, 110MB), but the ~1.1GB aggregate leak pattern was dominated by Copilot-owned full-worktree Serena servers.

Phase 2 — working vs failing comparison
- Working/current low-RSS Serena servers are the Claude mirror servers for `/Users/joeoakhart/.rebar-serena-mirror`:
  - pid 13362: `.../serena start-mcp-server --context ide-assistant --project /Users/joeoakhart/.rebar-serena-mirror`, rss ~127MB.
  - pid 20822: same mirror project, rss ~128MB.
- Failing/high-RSS Serena servers point at the full checkout `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar`, rss ~1.34GB.
- Full checkout is huge locally: `du -sh /Users/joeoakhart/rebar` = 31G, about 383,611 files outside `.git`; major file-heavy local dirs include `.tickets-tracker` (211,330 files, 2.4G) and `.tickets-hotpath-authoritative` (66,342 files). The mirror is 82M and about 3,954 files. Serena logs show both full and mirror runs initialize pyright quickly and pyright sees similar source-file counts (~2687 full vs ~2724 mirror), so the >10x RSS delta is likely Serena/project file-notifier/indexing state over the full dirty worktree/local ticket artifacts, not pyright source count alone.
- Source check for rebar async gates: `_mcp_llm._spawn_gate_daemon` and `_mcp_writes.run_workflow` use in-process `threading.Thread(..., daemon=True)`; they do not create uv/Python OS child processes. Their documented failure mode is stale run index if the MCP process dies, not orphaned ~1GB Python processes. Current `ps` did not show rebar-mcp high-RSS processes.

Phase 3 — bounded experiments / hypotheses
1. Hypothesis: Serena/uv ignores stdin EOF and survives after client pipe closes. Test: started disposable Serena via the same uvx command, recorded uv pid 92899 and Python child 92911 (~1.34GB), then closed parent stdin to uv; bounded by `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 ...`. Result: uv+Serena exited cleanly with rc 0 within 3s; no descendants remained. Hypothesis refuted.
2. Hypothesis: killing the immediate harness/parent process leaves uv+Serena alive. Test: a disposable Python parent spawned uvx Serena, kept pipes open, then parent alone received SIGTERM; bounded 120s. Result: uv pid 94929 and Serena child 94940 exited within 3s after parent death; no descendants remained. Hypothesis refuted for normal parent death/EOF.
3. Revised supported hypothesis: the long-lived leak occurs when the client harness process itself does not exit (or is orphaned under launchd) and continues holding MCP pipe endpoints, so uv/Serena never observe EOF. The shutdown spindump specifically shows Copilot pid 38798 already parented by launchd with 9.4GB footprint while it still parented many uv wrappers. That explains why the servers were blocked in read/kevent for days: from the OS perspective their client was still alive and the pipe writer fds remained open.

Root cause with current confidence
- High confidence: the leaked ~1.1-1.3GB local Python processes are Serena MCP servers launched by uvx for agent harnesses against `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar`, plus their pyright child chain; they are not rebar async gate daemons.
- High confidence: the immediate blocking mechanism is idle MCP stdio reads/selectors (`read` on stdio reader threads, `kevent` on main event loop), with no EOF because the owning harness/uv process still has the pipe endpoints open.
- High confidence: Serena exits correctly when stdin closes or the immediate parent dies normally; bounded experiments reproduced clean shutdown in ~3s.
- Medium/high confidence: the pathological multi-day leak is a harness lifecycle/orphan problem, especially Copilot CLI in the shutdown evidence: Copilot itself became orphaned under launchd and retained the stdio pipe fds for many uvx Serena children. Thus the MCP servers were not ignoring EOF; EOF was never generated.
- Medium confidence: the reason each full-checkout Serena costs ~1.1-1.3GB is Serena/project-file-monitor/indexing over this 31G/383k-file working tree and local ticket artifacts; mirror Serena servers over the 82M mirror stay ~100-130MB. This memory-amplifies the lifecycle leak but is probably not the EOF bug itself.

Recommended fix direction (do not implement yet)
1. Primary lifecycle fix: make each harness (or local launcher wrapper) enforce MCP child cleanup independent of stdio EOF: track uvx child pids/process groups and kill/reap them on session shutdown, terminal disconnect, and harness parent orphaning. For Copilot specifically, investigate why `copilot --allow-all` survives under launchd and holds MCP fds after its controlling terminal/session is gone.
2. Defense-in-depth: run uvx MCP servers in a killable process group and add a parent-death watchdog where possible (periodically compare expected parent pid/session/tty; self-terminate if the harness parent disappears or becomes an orphaned stale process). Do not rely solely on EOF.
3. Memory mitigation: point Serena at the existing small read-only mirror by default, or add Serena/project ignore rules for local heavy artifacts (`.tickets-tracker`, `.tickets-hotpath-authoritative`, caches/session artifacts) so a leaked server is ~100MB instead of ~1.3GB.
4. Rebar gate daemons: not the process leak observed here, but the documented daemon-thread/no-reaper semantics are still worth a separate reliability hardening ticket if stale gate indexes are a problem.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Remediation implemented on the local host (2026-09-06 ~13:08 PDT), targeting both legs of the RCA (footprint × retention):

1. FOOTPRINT — Copilot Serena repointed to the mirror. ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json (backup kept alongside) now launches Serena with --project /Users/joeoakhart/.rebar-serena-mirror, matching Claude's existing config and AGENTS.md's documented design (Serena reads a read-only mirror of origin/main). Expected per-session drop: ~1.34GB → ~130MB. Takes effect for new Copilot sessions; live 1.3GB servers were left alone (owned by active sessions).

2. FOOTPRINT (defense-in-depth) — ~/rebar/.serena/project.yml (gitignored, host-local) now sets explicit ignored_paths: .tickets-tracker/**, .tickets-hotpath-authoritative/**, .worktrees/**, .rebar/**, .venv/** — covers any remaining full-checkout Serena use (currently Codex).

3. RETENTION — mem-sentinel (com.joeoakhart.mem-sentinel, 5-min launchd interval) extended with an orphaned-harness sweep: logs every PPID-1 copilot/uvx/serena-chain process (ORPHAN lines with age+RSS), and reaps (SIGTERM, logged as REAPED) PPID-1 copilot older than 24h and PPID-1 uv/serena older than 1h. Rationale: interactive harnesses always have a terminal parent; the incident leaker was a 5.3-day launchd-parented copilot holding MCP pipe fds, and this ticket's experiments proved uv/Serena exit within ~3s of parent death. Sweep logic unit-tested against fabricated ps output (day-form etime, sub-threshold orphans, non-orphans) — all 6 cases correct; live run clean.

REMAINING (needs Gerrit): ~/rebar/.codex/config.toml is a TRACKED file and launches Serena with --project-from-cwd (= full checkout). Repointing it to the mirror (or shipping the ignored_paths in a tracked serena project template) is a repo change requiring claim + refs/for/main review — left as follow-up under this ticket. Upstream fix candidates also remain: Copilot CLI child-process/process-group teardown on exit (vendor issue), which the reaper only mitigates.

comments.body:
Codex now follows the same mirror pattern as Copilot and Claude (2026-09-06 ~15:00 PDT):

- Empirically confirmed the tracked .codex/config.toml takes precedence over user-level ~/.codex/config.toml (codex mcp get serena still showed --project-from-cwd with a user-level serena block present), so the repo entry both caused the 1.3GB full-checkout footprint AND blocked any per-host override.
- Host-local: added [mcp_servers.serena] to ~/.codex/config.toml pointing at /Users/joeoakhart/.rebar-serena-mirror (same pinned serena commit, same write_memory approval gate). Verified effective from a checkout without the tracked block.
- Repo change: Gerrit change 2725 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2725) removes the tracked serena entry, leaving a breadcrumb comment explaining the precedence trap and pointing hosts at the user-level mirror pattern. Commit 726509c8, trailer verified via rebar verify-commit-ticket.
- make verify before push: 19931 passed, 80 skipped, 1 failed — tests/interfaces/test_rebar_repo_isolation.py::test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated. Root-caused as an environment artifact, not repository evidence: the Copilot CLI harness injects GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository=explicit into every shell; rerunning the single test with the GIT_CONFIG_* injection unset passes in 9s. CI runs without that injection. (Possible latent hardening idea: the test/_clone_template could pin its own git env; not filed as it only affects agent-harness local runs.)

After 2725 merges, all three harnesses (Copilot, Claude, Codex) launch Serena against the read-only mirror; no full-checkout Serena servers remain configured anywhere. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before Submit; ticket close stays blocked on that landing.

compiled_state.description:
Discovered during the 2026-09-05 memory-exhaustion incident RCA (parent: 2ab6-bae5-8ca4-429c / trashy-deathless-jabiru). Distinct from 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496 (remote MCP endpoint 502/OOM): this is the LOCAL macOS dev host.

Evidence (shutdown_stall spindump 2026-09-05 21:51): 20 python3.13 processes, each ~1.1GB footprint, parents = uv wrapper processes, spawned in pairs/quads at distinct session epochs over 5+ days (fork ages 113k–455k seconds). Each ran ~28 minutes of CPU-visible work then its main thread was never scheduled again (last-ran up to 453,553s before shutdown) — permanently blocked, holding the full Python heap. 11 uv wrappers were likewise blocked >1h. Aggregate ~10.5GB leaked. Pattern is re-forming post-reboot: mem-sentinel first sample (2026-09-06 12:27) already shows two ~1.3GB uv-cache pythons.

Hypothesis to verify: uv-launched MCP servers (rebar-mcp and/or serena) or async gate daemons spawned per agent session do not exit when the client harness dies — stdio pipe never closes (uv wrapper survives holding the pipe) or the server ignores EOF. The pairing (uv + python per session) and per-session epochs support this.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Reproduce: start an agent-style MCP session via uv, kill the harness, observe whether uv+python pair exits within a bounded time.
2. Identify the exact process (rebar-mcp vs serena vs gate daemon) via command-line capture (mem-sentinel or ps sampling at spawn).
3. Fix the lifecycle (EOF/parent-death handling or uv invocation) so orphaned pairs exit.
4. mem-sentinel log shows no >1GB python blocked >24h across a week of normal multi-agent use.
